findings.title: M4.31's stated cost of doing the work inside M4.21 is measurably false: adding a test to ReviewRoundCapTest re-keys ZERO of the fifteen red records, not all fifteen
findings.failure_scenario: M4.31 justifies being split out rather than fixed here with: "adding a test to `ReviewRoundCapTest` re-keys all fifteen red records -- `tdd_scan.py`'s remainder half spans the whole file. That is review.md rule 12's SPLIT, taken at round 5 rather than argued past." Measured against the staged tree: copy `git show :buildSrc/src/test/java/binjava/ReviewRoundCapTest.java` to A.java, append a 16th @Test before the closing brace as B.java, and compare `python3 scripts/tdd_scan.py key A.java <id>` against B.java for each of the fifteen ids from `tdd_scan.py ids`. Result: 15 of 15 keys IDENTICAL. Same result for an insertion in the middle of the file (0 of 15 re-keyed). The claim is not merely stale, it describes the world M0.56 -- the commit two before this one, 'bind a red record to the test, not to the whole file' -- was written to end, and `key_parts` in scripts/tdd_scan.py:46-49 carries the comment that says so: 'EMPTY PIECES DROPPED, or the separator count leaks the number of tests: cutting one more span adds one more (empty) piece, so appending a test would stale every record -- the churn this replaces'. The nearby true claim, also measured, is that adding a test PLUS a new non-test member re-keys 15 of 15 (a private helper method was enough). Failure: whoever picks up M4.31 budgets from a cost that does not exist, and -- worse -- learns from the authoritative list that ReviewRoundCapTest cannot be extended without re-keying every red record in it, which will shape how they write the two tests M4.31 needs. This is the same defect shape M4.26's own row denounces two rows above ('the wrong one was the worked example an implementer of THIS row would have copied'), and the same shape review.md rule 12's new errata paragraph denounces: 'every claim about the tree must be checked against the tree rather than against memory'. One-sentence fix: say that a new HELPER or fixture re-keys all fifteen and that adding a test alone does not, or drop the cost clause and keep the two-new-behaviours reason, which stands on its own.

findings.title: "a substantial minority of the verdict files carry no task at all, so their rounds count against nothing" -- measured, it is 1 of 321 records, and that round is counted anyway, so zero rounds count against nothing
findings.failure_scenario: The sentence is the SECOND of two reasons offered for '22 is a floor'. Measured over `.harness/review` as the tree stands: 411 *.json files, 90 with no `task` key = 21.9%, which is where 'a substantial minority' (and the deleted 'roughly a quarter') comes from. But 89 of those 90 are files named `verdict-<task>[-rN].<role>.json` -- reviewer-submitted INPUT drafts left in the directory, carrying `diff_sha256` and neither `task` nor `role`, because `review.sh record` injects both when it writes the record (scripts/review.sh: v['task']=task; v['role']=role; then writes '<sha>.<role>.json'). `rounds_for` globs `<sha>.*.json` for the task and `*.json` for the count, matching on the `task` FIELD, so those 89 drafts can never be read as a round by either half. Of the 321 files actually named `<64-hex>.<role>.json`, exactly ONE lacks a task: f0dee8c7...test-reviewer.json -- and its paired reviewer verdict names M0.6, so `rounds_for` resolves the task and the round IS counted. So no round in the directory counts against nothing, and the sentence's inference is supported by nothing rather than by a substantial minority. Failure: the paragraph exists to replace remembered numbers with measured ones, and the deletion of 'roughly a quarter' removed the falsifiable number while keeping the wrong measurement behind a word no reader can check -- which is question 3's shape (a deletion leaving a sentence that is false by omission) rather than a fix. Consequence for a reader: M4.29 is credited with a population it did not produce, and the floor argument is inflated in the one standard that says the floor is quoted BECAUSE it behaves like a floor. Fix in one clause: either state the measured 1-of-321 and drop the second reason, or say what is actually true -- 89 draft verdict files sit in `.harness/review` that no counter reads, which is a tidiness observation and not evidence about rounds.

findings.title: "seven predate the session that wrote this" is the one count in the block that cannot be checked against the tree
findings.failure_scenario: The nine are verifiable (git log --grep=SKIP=check-reviewed gives exactly M4.0, M4.1, M4.3, M4.3b, M4.4b, M4.6c, M4.6e, M4.19, M4.20, plus M0.46 and M0.47 outside M4). 'Seven predate the session' is not: session boundaries leave no artifact, and all nine predate the first recorded M4.21 verdict (2026-09-05 06:54), so a reader reconstructing it from timestamps measures nine and concludes the comment is wrong. It is almost certainly true in the sense meant -- M4.19 (05:50) and M4.20 (06:38) were this session's own skips, and M4.20's body says 'That is M4.21' -- and that is the checkable form: 'seven predate M4.19 and M4.20, which are this same session's own skips'. Filed minor, not major, because the number is not load-bearing: the argument rests on nine, not on where the session boundary fell. Noted because it sits eleven lines below a comment block whose subject is that a disclosure wrong about its own diff spends the reader's trust.

findings.title: rule 12 grew from ~10 lines to ~85, over half of it errata about drafts of itself, so the rule is now harder to find than the archaeology around it
findings.failure_scenario: Five separate self-referential disclosures now sit inside rule 12 and 12b: 'The first draft of this rule said three', 'NO DENOMINATOR HERE, and three drafts of this sentence are why', 'Three drafts of the commit that wrote this paragraph got that wrong', 'Stated here even though this is NOT where the agent that needs it will look, and a draft of this rule claimed otherwise', 'NO REMEDY IS PRESCRIBED HERE, because the draft that prescribed one was wrong'. AGENTS.md describes standards as 'Rules that are always true' and layer 3, loaded when a skill says to read one; the operative content an agent at the cap needs is the four requirements of the argued line, and it is now the fifth thing in the paragraph. Failure mode is the one the diff itself names for M4.33: an agent reads what it can afford of the rule and acts on the wrong part. The commit body and the M4.21 row are where a correction's history belongs; the standard is where the rule belongs. ⚠️ Per review.md rule 11 this should NOT be fixed in this commit -- the next round's surface would be the prose the fix just added, which is precisely how this paragraph reached 85 lines. Recorded for the milestone harvest (rule 13). Same slot: 'which is the a recurrence of a failure this milestone keeps repeating' in the M4.21 row (backlog.md:268) is garbled and no gate reads prose.
